title: The Win32 redacted export projection has no browser-reachable surface, so the masking/idempotence contract cannot be verified from the app
expected: CSV: "redacted_export_projection masks only values the analyzer classified Sensitive ... Public records export unchanged, the projection is deterministic and repeatable, and applying it to an already projected analysis changes nothing." Entry point: parser crate API redacted_export_projection(&Win32Analysis).
observed: The projection is crate-internal: crates/cmtraceopen-parser/src/intune/apps/windows/win32/redaction.rs exports it (re-exported from win32/mod.rs) and only crate tests and the crate's own reducers call it. No Tauri command consumer exists (src-tauri/src/lib.rs invoke_handler has none), no wasm/TS binding exists, and no store field or UI action carries a Win32Analysis, so nothing rendered in the browser can exercise the projection. The only redaction surfaces the frontend can reach are redact_dsregcmd_status_text (dsregcmd) and export_esp_session (ESP), both of which belong to other stories/areas.
evidence: `grep -rn redacted_export_projection src-tauri crates`: hits only inside crates/cmtraceopen-parser (src + tests). `grep -rn "cmtraceopen_parser" src/`: no frontend reference to the parser crate. Spec: test '[INTUNE-038] the Win32 redacted export projection is unreachable from the browser' is test.fixme.

title: Swim-lane hover readout unreachable: BrushOverlay covered the canvas
expected: Hovering a lane bucket shows '<n> rows · <m> errors' in the corner readout; leaving the lanes clears it.
observed: BrushOverlay renders position:absolute; inset:0 above SwimLaneCanvas without pointer-events, so the canvas never received mousemove: the readout never rendered and the canvas double-click hook could not fire.
evidence: e2e/stories/timeline-events.spec.ts '[TL-007] hovering a bucket reports its row and error counts' (RED before the fix, green after); document.elementFromPoint at the lane centre resolved to the overlay div.
resolution: SwimLaneCanvas exposes a bucketAtPoint hit test through a ref; BrushOverlay forwards pointer position/leave, and TimelineWorkspace owns the readout. Dead canvas hover props removed.

title: Debug IPC bridge answered a request split across TCP segments as a parse error
expected: POST /invoke returns {result} for a well-formed call, with an explicit error only for unsupported or malformed input.
observed: handle_connection performed a single socket read, so a request whose body arrived in a second segment produced 'request parse error: EOF while parsing a value' (or reset the connection); roughly one in four calls failed against the live app.
evidence: src-tauri/src/ipc_bridge.rs unit tests: 'request_split_across_writes_is_served_in_full' (RED before, green after), 'whole_request_in_one_write_is_served', 'bodyless_get_is_served'; live probe: 30/30 sequential get_available_workspaces calls clean after the fix.
resolution: read_request loops until Content-Length is satisfied (bounded by MAX_REQUEST_BYTES); serve() split out of start() so the real handler is testable on an OS-assigned port.

title: Three browser-observable paths stay unverified: macOS log rescan, registry key search, registry per-path cache
expected: Rescan degrades every card to a placeholder; registry key search finds keys from the toolbar; re-opening a registry file restores it from the per-path cache without reparsing.
observed: Rescan did not replace the store's scan (files.length stayed 5); registry key search has no caller outside the store (setSearchQuery/searchNext/searchPrevious/expandToPath) and KeyTree only reacts to selectedKeyPath; re-opening a second registry fixture never showed that file's counts.
evidence: e2e/stories/other-workspaces.spec.ts: '[MACDIAG-006] a rescan with no files degrades every card to a placeholder' and '[REG-002] the first open parses and auto-expands, a return to it is cached' are test.fixme with those reasons; REG-001 is static analysis of src/stores/registry-store.ts and src/components/registry-view/KeyTree.tsx.
resolution: Recorded as coverage gaps with error_class=harness; the sibling assertions in both specs do pass, so the surrounding behaviour is verified and only these paths are not.

title: Secure Boot banner's scanning affordance was dead code
expected: The banner reports an in-progress scan: a disabled Rescan that reads 'Scanning…', plus the scan-timestamp line.
observed: While a scan runs SecureBootWorkspace replaces the whole results state — banner included — with a centred spinner, so StatusBanner's isScanning branch ('Scanning…', disabled Rescan) and its scanTimestamp line can never render; the scanTimestamp prop is never passed by the workspace.
evidence: e2e/stories/other-workspaces.spec.ts '[SB-011] the banner reports the in-progress scan and disables Rescan' (test.fixme, reason recorded): no element reading 'Scanning…' is in the DOM during a deferred rescan, while the sibling test observes the analysing spinner copy 'Running detection script...' and the disabled action buttons.
resolution: The unreachable banner branch and its unused prop are removed; the workspace's analysing spinner is the single scanning affordance, and SB-011's contract text is corrected to match.

title: Story specs inherited the development host's date/time format from the debug bridge
expected: The browser harness emulates a Windows host, so rendered Date/Time columns follow the Windows preferences the shim publishes, with or without the debug IPC bridge.
observed: Once the bridge answered get_system_date_time_preferences with the real host's answer, a macOS development host rendered ISO timestamps where the shim's Windows contract (M/d/yyyy h:mm:ss tt) was expected: [LOG-083]'s row assertion failed 2/2 in the retest while CI stayed green.
evidence: e2e/stories/log-view.spec.ts '[LOG-083] the info pane summarises the parser that read the file': received 'Line 1 | Error | AppEnforce | 2031-10-04 12:00:00…' instead of the emulated-Windows pattern.
resolution: bootApp pins get_system_date_time_preferences to the Windows defaults by default; a spec that is about the format itself (CHROME-059) still overrides it by name.

title: e2e/esp-diagnostics.spec.ts read the host's elevation state, so it failed with the app running
expected: The ESP spec renders the Windows administrator-coverage surface deterministically, with or without the debug IPC bridge.
observed: The spec never stubbed get_esp_elevation_state, so with `npm run app:dev` running the real backend answered restartSupported=false on macOS and the 'Restart as administrator' button these tests assert disappeared (1 of 13 failed; CI is green because it has no bridge).
evidence: e2e/esp-diagnostics.spec.ts: 1 failed / 12 passed with the app running before, 13 passed after.
resolution: The spec extends its page fixture with an init-script override that pins the elevation probe to the Windows-stub value, matching the shim's static default.

title: Debug bridge startup commands were unimplemented, so a browser session booted with console errors
expected: With `npm run app:dev` running, a browser session against :1420 boots clean: the debug bridge answers the same startup questions the real backend does.
observed: take_second_launch_paths, get_initial_elevation_restore, sync_app_menu_state and get_system_date_time_preferences were not implemented, so the app logged '[file-association] failed to claim a forwarded launch … Command take_second_launch_paths failed.' and three warnings at boot; e2e/smoke.spec.ts ('app loads at :1420 without JS errors') failed 2/2 while the app was running.
evidence: e2e/smoke.spec.ts: 2 failed / 29 passed before, 5 passed after the fix with the app running; src-tauri/src/ipc_bridge.rs test 'debug_bridge_answers_browser_session_startup_commands' pins the four responses.

title: Collector Pester suite failed on any host whose UTC offset is not zero
expected: scripts/collection/tests/Invoke-CmtraceEvidenceCollection.Tests.ps1 passes wherever it runs.
observed: 1 of 29 tests failed on this host (UTC-0400): the bundle-id test mocked a local-kind DateTime while New-CollectorBundleId stamps UTC, so the expectation encoded the runner's timezone.
evidence: pwsh Invoke-Pester before: 28 passed / 1 failed ('uses the invariant Gregorian calendar under a non-Gregorian culture'); with TZ=UTC: 29 passed; after the fix on the local timezone: 29 passed.
resolution: The test's mocked clock is an explicit UTC instant, so the assertion no longer depends on the host offset.

title: Timeline rendered 'Not Reported' rows, making the documented empty state unreachable
expected: Timeline rows are omitted when they have no value; with nothing timestamped the section shows 'No timeline-friendly timestamps were found in this capture.'
observed: Previous PRT attempt, Azure AD PRT update and Client reference time fell back to formatValue(null) => 'Not Reported', so those rows survived the empty-value filter and the empty-state branch was dead code.
evidence: e2e/stories/diagnostics.spec.ts '[DSREG-017] the timeline omits rows without a timestamp and shows its empty state' (RED before, green after).
resolution: buildTimelineItems uses a timelineTimestamp helper that returns an empty string for absent values (keeping raw text for unparsable ones), so the existing filter drops those rows.

title: Capture-confidence qualifier mangled acronyms and skipped two conclusion boxes
expected: Every conclusion box carries the 'Based on this capture, …' qualifier below High confidence, with the original copy intact.
observed: qualifyByCaptureConfidence lower-cased the first character of the detail, rendering 'mDM visibility…', 'pRT present…', 'nGC is Yes…'; Current phase and Join posture never carried the qualifier at all.
evidence: e2e/stories/diagnostics.spec.ts '[DSREG-018] every conclusion flow box is confidence-qualified' (red before, green after); the pre-existing test used case-insensitive regexes, which hid the mangling.

title: Quick Stats severity card was never marked active, so it could not be toggled off
expected: Clicking a severity card filters the list and outlines the card in the severity colour (2px); clicking it again clears the filter.
observed: The card set filteredIds directly, but the external-clear effect tested hasActiveFilter() (clauses only), so it reset activeSeverity on the same commit: the outline stayed 1px and a second click re-applied instead of clearing.
evidence: e2e/stories/log-view.spec.ts '[LOG-053] the active severity card shows its outline and toggles off' (RED before, green after).
resolution: The card records the ids it applied and the effect resets the card only when the store's filteredIds is null or a different set (an external filter change or clear).

title: Sidebar 'Merge into Timeline' merged without clearing the active filter
expected: The sidebar merge clears the active filter first, like the sibling select-file and reload-source actions.
observed: The button's onClick collected cached paths and called createMergedTab without clearFilter, so clause filters from the previous view survived into the merged stream.
evidence: e2e/stories/log-view.spec.ts '[LOG-058] the sidebar merge clears the active filter first' (RED before, green after): clauses stayed [{Message contains A-line}] after the merge.
resolution: clearFilter() runs before createMergedTab in the Merge loaded files handler.

story_ids: CHROME-048, CHROME-038, CHROME-058, LOG-*, DSREG-*, TL-*
title: Story specs could assert a shadow store instance after any source edit
expected: A spec that seeds or reads a Vite module acts on the instance the running app holds.
observed: After an edit, Vite serves invalidated modules under '?t=' URLs, which are distinct module instances: import('/src/stores/ui-store.ts') from a spec seeded a second store while the app rendered the first (proved: sidebarCollapsed=true did not collapse the sidebar; seedStore-based assertions failed only in that session state).
evidence: PROBE output: sameInstance=false for '/src/stores/ui-store.ts?probe=1'; performance resource entries showed the app loading '/src/stores/ui-store.ts?t=1790281443518' while the spec imported the bare path; seeding sidebarCollapsed left the sidebar expanded.
resolution: seedStore applies state to every loaded instance of the module, and bootApp fails loudly when HMR-timestamped URLs are present so a stale session cannot silently test a shadow instance; the authoritative runs restart the dev server (as CI does).

title: Known-source family expansion: missing direct paths and unavailable folders are not asserted
expected: Opening a family verifies each direct file path, skips missing or inaccessible ones, keeps only pattern-matching folder entries and warns per unavailable folder.
observed: Covered end to end for present sources; the skip/warn branches have no browser assertion.
evidence: e2e/stories/log-view.spec.ts '[LOG-086] known sources are grouped, and Open all expands a family' (passes).
resolution: Retained as a documented coverage gap; the branches need a filesystem-backed fixture to be exercised honestly.

title: File-association prompt status is verified only through sibling module tests
expected: supported=true on Windows with shouldPrompt = not suppressed and not registered; false off Windows.
observed: get_file_association_prompt_status needs a Tauri AppHandle, so no focused unit test covers the status computation; the handler tests cover registry readback and visible registration.
evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/file_association.rs tests visible_registration_requires_the_expected_name_and_a_description and registry_readback_only_treats_missing_entries_as_unregistered (pass).
resolution: Recorded as partial evidence; a focused test needs an AppHandle or a pure status helper extracted from the command.

title: Registered IPC commands with no frontend caller, and known-source type fields nothing reads
expected: Every registered command and public type field has a consumer.
observed: 11 registered commands have no frontend reference (close_timeline_cmd, evtx_capture/export/import/load_provider_databases, evtx_loaded_map_count, evtx_provider_databases, get_esp_diagnostics_capability, lookup_error_code), and types/log.ts declares defaultFileIntent/preferredFileNames that neither Rust nor the frontend produces or reads.
evidence: Static scan of src/**/*.ts(x) against the app_invoke_handler! list (0 frontend-only commands, 11 backend-only); grep for defaultFileIntent/preferredFileNames finds only the type declarations.
resolution: Retained deliberately: the evtx_* commands are exercised by the Rust suite and the provider-database/map loaders are startup/admin surfaces; removing them is a separate design decision, not a defect fix.
